pages.text: "Here comes the boat!" Lolo in yellow boots splashed into a puddle at the pier's end. A boat from the mainland reached the pier. Today, Grandma was visiting.

"We will show Grandma the shells we found!" Riri in her yellow hat counted shells in a basket. But when Grandma stepped off the boat, both grew shy. It had been so long that they hardly remembered her face.
"Oh, our Riri and Lolo have grown so much!" Grandma spread both arms. But Riri hid behind the basket, and Lolo behind the rope post. "H-hello..." The greeting disappeared beneath the waves' sound.
Even at home, they sat together in a corner opposite the stove. Grandma's bundle smelled unlike anything in their house. All the way home, neither had held her hand.
Grandma opened the bundle, revealing steaming bread. "I baked it before boarding. Still warm, right?" One bite filled their mouths with sweetness.
"What is this?" Lolo pointed at yarn inside the bundle. "I brought it to knit your scarves. Come and sit." Grandma sat by the stove and patted her knees.
Riri quietly sat on her left knee, Lolo on her right. Grandma's lap was soft and warm. "Wow, Grandma's lap is the softest!" Lolo beamed.
Now they knew their places. One, Riri on the left! Two, Lolo on the right! Three, both snug on one lap! Knitting needles clattered as Grandma told old sea stories.
The next day, Grandma's boat was moored at the pier. Yesterday they had felt shy; today tears filled their eyes. "Grandma, come again! We will find more shells for you!"

Grandma hugged one with each arm, both wearing new scarves. Someone unfamiliar soon felt close when they ate and sat together. Burying their faces in the scarves, Riri and Lolo said, "Grandma's lap is the softest!"
